findings.issue: The pivot restores the BASE comment-blind gate (flags ANY occurrence of agent_instruction/agent-instruction in a non-allowlist src/http file, comment or code) and removes the false positive at the source by rewording the only two offending doc comments so they no longer contain the literal. This is structurally the most robust fix — with no comment/regex parser there is no evasion surface, so the R1/R2/R3 lexer false-negatives are impossible by construction. The only residual is a known, pre-existing maintenance trade-off inherent to the BASE gate: a FUTURE legit comment in some non-allowlist src/http file that again mentions 'agent_instruction'/'agent-instruction' in prose would re-red the gate, and the next author would have to reword again (the same trap that opened T-0758). This is not a defect introduced by this change — it is the restored original design, and it errs in the SAFE direction (false-positive: the gate reds and a human looks, never a false-negative). Documented here only so the trade-off is visible for a possible future substrate task (e.g. an allowlist-comment convention). Reword doc-accuracy verified: 'the instruction-promote path in artifacts.ts' is correct — the promote path genuinely lives in src/http/artifacts.ts (CONFIG_TABLES includes agent_instruction; decidePromote/assertWritable/INSERT INTO choros.agent_instruction all in artifacts.ts), so the shortened wording still points to the right file and is not misleading.
findings.suggestion: None required for merge. Optional future hardening: a lightweight allowlist for whole-line doc comments that legitimately cross-reference agent_instruction in prose, so a comment-blind gate need not force rewording. Not in scope for T-0758.
